title: A trusted replay that diverges after a side effect hands the app its completed steps, and nothing is delivered twice
description: The app is the proving suite's FIXTURE APP: a fake harness that performs the goal's actions on the fake machine and reports each one as the cockpit does, through the same session writer a delegated app session is recorded through. It is not a provider and plays no cassette; every session it runs counts as one model reach, because an app session is the intelligence a learned procedure exists to stop paying for. The lifecycle climbs to trusted as in the amortized-cost scenario. In the measured goal the fake machine refuses the SECOND action once, after the trusted replay has already delivered the first -- a notice. The replay must stop there and hand the goal to the app with the completed step and its idempotency key; the app honours that guidance, so the fake machine -- which records a duplicate rather than refusing one -- must see every side effect exactly once. The app's repair session is recorded like any other, and the lifecycle does NOT learn from it: the measured goal is the last, and what the learner makes of a repair is no figure this scenario publishes.
